one_month_reasoning: The key event in the window is the fiscal Q1 FY27 report: the quarter closed 2026-10-02 (10-K/fiscal calendar), and Seagate reported Q1 a year ago on 2025-10-28, so results are very likely due about 2026-10-27/28, inside the window. Guidance is $4.1B +/- $0.1B revenue and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS. The company beat the top of its range in Q4 FY26, says it has build-to-order contracts covering all of calendar 2027 and that most nearline exabytes are allocated into calendar 2028, so a beat and a Q2 guide-up are likely. The market will mostly be listening for management's answer on the Toshiba capacity news (Nikkei, 2026-10-02: about Y60B to double HDD capacity in the Philippines by FY2027, with a 30% share goal). Management should say again that Toshiba buys heads and media from outside suppliers, which caps the real exabyte supply (Citi made the same point), and that its own pricing is locked through 2027. That favours a partial rebound after an 11% one-day drop that was driven by sentiment. Against that, the stock rose from about $803 on 2026-09-22 to $945.57 on 2026-10-01, so positioning was crowded. I use a monthly vol of about 21% (75%/3.5) and put the median slightly above spot (about $845) for the likely beat and partial reversal. P(close >= 837.52) = 0.52, which is close to neutral on purpose.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $50, a haircut to FY28 consensus of $55.37, x 17 = $850) and FCF yield (FY28 FCF about $9.5B / 230M shares = $41.3 per share at a 5% yield = $826). Weighted 60/40, which gives about $840-850.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (roughly FY28, Jul-2027 to Jun-2028) $50 x 17x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus of $55.37 cut about 10%. Pricing growth of 20%+ YoY (the Q1 guide, per call) is unlikely to persist into 2028 once Toshiba adds capacity and contracts reprice. Management says nearline exabyte growth will be mid-20s with flat units, and the Q4 exit run-rate is about $7.3-8 per quarter, so $50 needs about $12.5 per quarter by mid-FY28, which is plausible if margins hold near 55-58%.

Today the stock trades at about 23x FY27 consensus ($838/$35.78). HDD makers have historically traded around 8-15x at cycle peaks. 17x is above that history because of LTA visibility into 2028 and 90% data-center mix, but it compresses as earnings are expected to be closer to peak and new supply (Toshiba) arrives.

inputs_detail.value: 231M (Q1 FY27 guide), about 230M by FY28 with buybacks
inputs_detail.derivation: 226.8M basic at 2026-07-03, plus 1.65M issued on the Sep-2026 note exchange; the notes are now retired, so the convert dilution ends. Buybacks continue from a $4.8B authorization.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF about $9.5B / 230M shares = $41.3 per share, capitalised at a 5% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 FY27 guide is $4.1B with sequential growth guided all year, so FY27 is about $18-19B. FY28 is about +12% on mid-20s exabyte growth, partly offset by slower pricing. A ~50% op margin (Q1 guide), a 16% tax rate and 5% capex give an FCF margin of about 45%.
Today's implied FY27 FCF yield is about 3.5-4% at $838. I require a higher yield of 5% at the horizon for cyclical-peak risk and a 14% single-customer concentration (10-K).

bear.story: Toshiba and WDC capacity additions plus a hyperscaler capex pause make the market expect nearline pricing to roll over in calendar 2028 contract talks. EPS momentum stalls and the market prices STX as a peak-cycle HDD maker (about 10x on about $43 NTM EPS). This is consistent with past HDD drawdowns and with the 52-week low of $209.

base.story: Contracts deliver as guided (sequential growth through FY27, EPS about $36), Mozaic 4/5 keeps the cost-per-TB lead, and pricing growth slows to mid-single digits in 2028. The multiple compresses from about 23x to about 17x on NTM EPS of about $50-52, so the price ends roughly flat.

bull.story: AI inference/KV-cache and physical-AI data retention keep exabyte demand above supply. Toshiba's expansion is limited by head and media supply, LTAs extend into 2029 at higher prices, FY28 EPS reaches $60+, and the market holds about 22x.

thesis_break_reason: Around $520 (-38%, and below the bear-case EPS times a normal-peak 12x) the market would be pricing a real break in the contract/pricing thesis: falling price per exabyte in new LTAs, a hyperscaler pushing out or cancelling build-to-order volumes, or a Mozaic 4/5 yield or qualification slip. That is a regime change from 'allocated into 2028', not ordinary 75%-vol noise.

How long price-per-exabyte growth lasts (about 10% YoY in June, 20%+ implied by the September guide) and what multiple the market pays as earnings near peak

reasoning: Primary documents show a business at record earnings with unusually good visibility. Q4 FY26: revenue $3.63B (+48% YoY), non-GAAP GM 52.7%, EPS $5.71, FCF $1.1B. The Q1 FY27 guide is $4.1B and $7.30 EPS at about a 50% op margin, and management guides sequential revenue and margin growth through FY27. The call says contracts cover all of calendar 2027 with pricing set, most nearline exabytes are allocated into 2028, and price per exabyte rose about 10% YoY in June and accelerates in the September guide. The balance sheet is de-levering: debt is about $2.4B after Q1 and the 2028 exchangeables were settled on 2026-09-08 with 1.65M shares issued (8-K). The 2026-10-02 drop of about 11% (from $945.57) was caused by a Nikkei report that Toshiba will invest about Y60B to double HDD capacity in the Philippines by FY2027 and aims for 30% share from just over 10% (Investing.com, 24/7 Wall St.). That is a credible medium-term threat to the supply discipline that drives current pricing. It does not touch reported or contracted 2027 numbers, and Citi argues Toshiba is limited by outside head and media supply. I treat it as raising the odds that pricing fades in 2028, not as an immediate hit. Valuation: the stock is at about 23x FY27 consensus ($35.78) and about 15x FY28 ($55.37). With a haircut NTM EPS of $50 at the horizon and a de-rating to 17x, plus a 5% FCF-yield cross-check, fair value is about $845, essentially flat versus $837.52. So I centre the median at about $850. For the spread I use an effective vol of about 62%, a bit below the realized 75% because earnings visibility is high, but I keep fat tails: the stock went from $209 to $1,145 in a year, and HDD history includes 50%+ drawdowns when pricing turns. Scenario mean is about $880 (25% at $430 / 50% at $870 / 25% at $1,350). Research was limited to company filings, the call transcript and a few news reports; the Toshiba release itself was not found in Toshiba's own channels (Nikkei-sourced).
